lines.text: Ella makes her drink stronger by pouring in more juice AND more water.
lines.caption: Ella makes her drink stronger by pouring in more juice AND more water.

lines.text: Lots of kids find the juice. <short pause> But this question asks about the water!
lines.caption: Lots of kids find the juice. But this question asks about the water!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's keep the juice and the water apart.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's keep the juice and the water apart.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Ella has twenty liters of a drink that is thirty percent juice.
lines.caption: Ella has twenty liters of a drink that is thirty percent juice.

lines.text: She adds some pure juice and some water.
lines.caption: She adds some pure juice and some water.

lines.text: Now she has twenty-five liters of a drink that is forty percent juice.
lines.caption: Now she has twenty-five liters of a drink that is forty percent juice.

lines.text: How many liters of water does she add?
lines.caption: How many liters of water does she add?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? There are two drinks: the one she starts with, and the one she ends with.
lines.caption: So what do we know? There are two drinks: the one she starts with, and the one she ends with.

lines.text: Each drink is part juice, part water. Thirty percent juice means thirty parts in every hundred.
lines.caption: Each drink is part juice, part water. Thirty percent juice means thirty parts in every hundred.

lines.text: She adds two things, juice and water. We want just the water.
lines.caption: She adds two things, juice and water. We want just the water.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: split each drink into juice and water.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: split each drink into juice and water.

lines.text: Start with the twenty liters. Ten percent of twenty is two, so thirty percent is six.
lines.caption: Start with the twenty liters. Ten percent of twenty is two, so thirty percent is six.

lines.text: So the first drink has six liters of juice.
lines.caption: So the first drink has six liters of juice.

lines.text: The rest is water. Twenty minus six is fourteen liters of water.
lines.caption: The rest is water. Twenty minus six is fourteen liters of water.

lines.text: Now the final drink: twenty-five liters that is forty percent juice.
lines.caption: Now the final drink: twenty-five liters that is forty percent juice.

lines.text: Forty percent is two fifths. One fifth of twenty-five is five, so two fifths is ten.
lines.caption: Forty percent is two fifths. One fifth of twenty-five is five, so two fifths is ten.

lines.text: So the final drink has ten liters of juice.
lines.caption: So the final drink has ten liters of juice.

lines.text: And twenty-five minus ten is fifteen liters of water.
lines.caption: And twenty-five minus ten is fifteen liters of water.

lines.text: Now line the two drinks up: juice next to juice, water next to water.
lines.caption: Now line the two drinks up: juice next to juice, water next to water.

lines.text: Juice goes from six to ten. So Ella adds four liters of juice.
lines.caption: Juice goes from six to ten. So Ella adds four liters of juice.

lines.text: Water goes from fourteen to fifteen. So she adds just one liter of water!
lines.caption: Water goes from fourteen to fifteen. So she adds just one liter of water!

lines.text: Check: four plus one is five, and twenty plus five is twenty-five. It fits!
lines.caption: Check: four plus one is five, and twenty plus five is twenty-five. It fits!

lines.text: The answer is one liter. That's Choice B!
lines.caption: The answer is one liter. That's Choice B!

lines.text: Here's a faster way. Forget the juice, and watch only the water.
lines.caption: Here's a faster way. Forget the juice, and watch only the water.

lines.text: If thirty percent is juice, then seventy percent is water.
lines.caption: If thirty percent is juice, then seventy percent is water.

lines.text: Ten percent of twenty is two, so seventy percent is fourteen liters of water.
lines.caption: Ten percent of twenty is two, so seventy percent is fourteen liters of water.

lines.text: In the final drink, forty percent is juice, so sixty percent is water.
lines.caption: In the final drink, forty percent is juice, so sixty percent is water.

lines.text: Sixty percent is three fifths. One fifth of twenty-five is five, so three fifths is fifteen liters of water.
lines.caption: Sixty percent is three fifths. One fifth of twenty-five is five, so three fifths is fifteen liters of water.

lines.text: Water goes from fourteen to fifteen. She adds one liter. Same answer!
lines.caption: Water goes from fourteen to fifteen. She adds one liter. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the question asks about one thing, follow just that one.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the question asks about one thing, follow just that one.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice D, four, is the juice she adds, not the water. Read what the question asks!
lines.caption: Choice D, four, is the juice she adds, not the water. Read what the question asks!

lines.text: Choice E, five, is everything she adds, juice and water together.
lines.caption: Choice E, five, is everything she adds, juice and water together.

lines.text: Choice A, zero, is what you'd get if you thought she adds only juice.
lines.caption: Choice A, zero, is what you'd get if you thought she adds only juice.

lines.text: But five liters of juice would give eleven liters of juice, not ten. Too strong!
lines.caption: But five liters of juice would give eleven liters of juice, not ten. Too strong!

lines.text: Choice C, two, is what you'd get from ten percent of twenty, the jump from thirty to forty percent.
lines.caption: Choice C, two, is what you'd get from ten percent of twenty, the jump from thirty to forty percent.

lines.text: But with two liters of water, she adds three of juice. That's only nine liters of juice, not ten.
lines.caption: But with two liters of water, she adds three of juice. That's only nine liters of juice, not ten.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Follow each part separately, and answer the exact question.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Follow each part separately, and answer the exact question.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new mix, and it's sneakier.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new mix, and it's sneakier.

lines.text: Leo has fifteen liters of a drink that is sixty percent juice.
lines.caption: Leo has fifteen liters of a drink that is sixty percent juice.

lines.text: He adds pure juice and water to make twenty-four liters that is fifty percent juice.
lines.caption: He adds pure juice and water to make twenty-four liters that is fifty percent juice.

lines.text: How many liters of juice does he add, and how many liters of water?
lines.caption: How many liters of juice does he add, and how many liters of water?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Sixty percent is three fifths. One fifth of fifteen is three, so three fifths is nine.
lines.caption: Let's check. Sixty percent is three fifths. One fifth of fifteen is three, so three fifths is nine.

lines.text: So Leo starts with nine liters of juice, and fifteen minus nine is six liters of water.
lines.caption: So Leo starts with nine liters of juice, and fifteen minus nine is six liters of water.

lines.text: The final drink is half juice. Half of twenty-four is twelve. So, twelve juice and twelve water.
lines.caption: The final drink is half juice. Half of twenty-four is twelve. So, twelve juice and twelve water.

lines.text: Juice goes from nine to twelve. He adds three liters of juice.
lines.caption: Juice goes from nine to twelve. He adds three liters of juice.

lines.text: Water goes from six to twelve. He adds six liters of water.
lines.caption: Water goes from six to twelve. He adds six liters of water.

lines.text: Check: three plus six is nine, and fifteen plus nine is twenty-four. It works!
lines.caption: Check: three plus six is nine, and fifteen plus nine is twenty-four. It works!

lines.text: Here's the sneaky part. The drink got weaker, but he still added some juice.
lines.caption: Here's the sneaky part. The drink got weaker, but he still added some juice.

lines.text: If you found three liters of juice and six liters of water, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found three liters of juice and six liters of water, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When you mix drinks, split each drink into its juice and its water.
lines.caption: When you mix drinks, split each drink into its juice and its water.

lines.text: Find how much of each the final drink needs. Then subtract what was already there.
lines.caption: Find how much of each the final drink needs. Then subtract what was already there.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
